title: Handshake State Merging (State Machine Contention)
damaged_code:
```rust
enum HandshakeState {
    REQ_ACK, // Merged Request and Acknowledgment state
    READY,
    IDLE,
}
```
pattern: A state machine enum merges two logically distinct phases of a handshake (such as request and acknowledgment) into a single combined state.
why_bad: Under concurrency, if a single merged state represents both the request and acknowledgment, the state can be accessed or written to by both the signal handler/interrupt and the fastpath thread simultaneously. This causes race conditions and state corruption that a four-state machine cleanly avoids.
detection: An enum representing handshake protocols combines consecutive transit states into a single variant.
counterexample:
Modeling the transition phases as distinct, separate states:
```rust
enum FineHandshakeState {
    REQUEST,
    ACKNOWLEDGE,
    READY,
    IDLE,
}
```
fix:
Separate the merged state into distinct enum variants to ensure clear, single-threaded ownership during transitions.
```rust
// Splitting REQ_ACK to REQ and ACK variants.
```
